scenario: [LGRA.5.8.6]: JSON text of exactly the text limit, 24,576 bytes, handed to a host parse, is admitted. The site is the cache seed ([NSTG.9.1]), the one place the harness hands a runtime JSON TEXT rather than a built value: `runner.py`'s `_cache_seeds` passes `json.dumps(value)`, which writes U+0001 as the six bytes `\u0001` and separates array items with `, `. The value is a two-item array: 2,233 repeats of U+0001 followed by `aaaaa` (11 bytes of text each), then `aaaaa`. Its text is 1 + (2 + 24,563) + 2 + (2 + 5) + 1 = 24,576 bytes, while the value is inside the three tree limits (depth 2, 3 nodes, 13,403 string bytes), so only the text limit could refuse it. The seed raises nothing and nothing is asserted (fact_count 0). Paired with LGRA.5.8.6_host_text_over_limit, whose last string is one byte longer, so a text limit of 24,575 (this vector goes red) or 24,577 (the other goes red) is caught. PATH PINNED: on libds, `ds_json_parse`'s `len > DS_JSON_MAX_TEXT_BYTES` test in pyds's `cache_seed`, then `ds_engine_cache_seed`. On the Mercury runtime, `test_behave.m` hands `ds.engine.seed_cache_text` the same `json.dumps` text, and `ds.json_text.parse` admits it on the same byte count.
